official_sources: Flood risk and coastal change planning guidance
NPPF chapter 14 flooding and coastal change

official_measurement_examples.name: National SMP coverage
official_measurement_examples.fact: Twenty Shoreline Management Plans cover the English coast and set management direction over short, medium and long-term horizons; they are strategic risk-management plans, not parcel planning permissions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Living-plan status
official_measurement_examples.fact: SMPs are living plans and management approaches can change when evidence or risk changes, so historic approach snapshots must retain date and version.

official_measurement_examples.name: Four management approaches
official_measurement_examples.fact: Hold the line, no active intervention, managed realignment and advance the line are management approaches; none by itself guarantees a funded defence scheme or parcel safety.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current erosion map horizons
official_measurement_examples.fact: The national coastal erosion service shows estimated risk to 2055 and 2105 under scenarios with and without planned shoreline management; scenario extent is not a certainty boundary.

official_measurement_examples.name: CCMA distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local planning authorities can use SMP evidence to designate Coastal Change Management Areas; an SMP policy unit and a CCMA are related but distinct planning geographies.

official_measurement_examples.name: Hold-line funding limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A hold-the-line policy can depend on future funding and implementation; the policy label must not be converted into a guaranteed defence-life assumption.

official_measurement_examples.name: Erosion versus flood zones
official_measurement_examples.fact: Coastal erosion risk is distinct from fluvial and tidal Flood Zone mapping and must not be collapsed into a single hazard class.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning lifetime assessment
official_measurement_examples.fact: Coastal planning decisions should consider management direction and risk over the anticipated development lifetime; current shoreline position alone is not a long-term buildability conclusion.

core_rules: SMP approach is not guaranteed defence delivery
SMP versions and changes retain date
CCMA is distinct from SMP policy unit
coastal erosion scenario is not certainty boundary
hold the line does not guarantee funding
erosion risk is distinct from flood zones
current shoreline is not long-term buildability proof
coastal policy does not determine ownership
coastal defence presence does not reserve development capacity
no parcel coastal clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
